record.paper_title: Open problems on billiards and geometric optics
record.original_question: For a centrally symmetric body such as an ellipse or a square, assume the body starts in pure rotation about its center with no translation in the Newtonian-aerodynamics model. Do the same conclusions sought for the rotating rod hold: is the total number of turns finite or infinite, does the angular velocity tend to zero, and what is its asymptotic behavior as t → +∞?

evidence.quote: More questions: A centrally symmetric body (for example, an ellipse, a square, etc.) starts the rotational motion around its center (no translation). The same questions as in the previous paragraph.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider the Newtonian (free molecular) aerodynamics model in the plane: a rarefied medium consists of point particles of negligible mass at rest, and a rigid convex body moves through them. When a particle meets the boundary of the body it undergoes a perfectly elastic collision (specular reflection in the body's instantaneous frame), thereby transferring momentum and angular momentum to the body; mutual interactions between particles are neglected. The body's motion is governed by the resulting force and torque on it.

Let B ⊂ ℝ² be a centrally symmetric convex body (for example an ellipse or a square), with center of mass at the origin and moment of inertia I about its center. Assume that at time t = 0 the center of B is at rest at the origin, and B has nonzero angular velocity ω(0) ≠ 0; the center is held (or, equivalently, by central symmetry the net aerodynamic force vanishes so that) the center does not translate, and the body undergoes pure rotation about its center under the torque exerted by collisions with the rarefied medium.

Determine:
(a) Whether the total angle ∫₀^∞ ω(t) dt swept by B is finite or infinite (i.e., whether the body performs only finitely many turns or infinitely many turns).
(b) Whether ω(t) → 0 as t → +∞.
(c) The precise asymptotic behavior of ω(t) as t → +∞.
artifact.status_search_result: The analogous problem for a rotating rod has been analyzed by Plakhov and collaborators, but no published resolution was found addressing the centrally symmetric body case (ellipse, square, etc.) under pure rotation in Newtonian aerodynamics. The question appears to remain open.

status_evidence.title: Motion of a rough disc in Newtonian aerodynamics
status_evidence.snippet: Studies trajectories of rough discs in rarefied media under Newtonian aerodynamics; does not resolve the asymptotic rotation problem for general centrally symmetric bodies.
status_evidence.claim: Related results exist for discs but do not address centrally symmetric body rotation asymptotics.

status_evidence.title: Billiard in a rotating half-plane
status_evidence.snippet: Asymptotic formulas for a uniformly rotating rod colliding elastically with a ball; related setting but for a rod rather than centrally symmetric body.
status_evidence.claim: The rod case is addressed; the centrally symmetric body case is not.
